title: EvoOtter: Evolutionary Reproduction Test Generator
read_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.02854 (v1, 03 July 2026; all 9,024 words, including methods, full evaluation, limitations and references)
datasets: SWT-Bench-Verified (433 instances; reported result, but not the main controlled evaluation)
task: Generate a bug-reproduction test (BRT) from an issue description and the old repository state. BRT must fail on buggy code and pass on the hidden fixed code (F2P). EvoOtter starts with heterogeneous-prompt candidates, localizes suspected focal functions, creates nine rule-based mutants, selects tests by normalized execution-log changes, and uses batched LLM crossover with successive halving.
input_setting: Repository-level Python issue-to-test generation on SWE-bench-derived datasets. The fixed patch is hidden at generation time and used as the F2P evaluation oracle. The paper's secondary SWT-Bench-Verified result is directly relevant to SWT reproduction, but the paper does not run on Defects4J/BugsInPy.
author_relationship_evidence: The paper and first-author Martin Hirzel's official publication page identify the same title/authors, but neither exposes a code/data repository link. Exact-title and author-plus-project GitHub searches found no attributable EvoOtter implementation. Paper states prompts are in supplementary material; prompts alone are not the implementation or evaluation artifact.
license: Paper is distributed under arXiv CC BY 4.0. No software license applies because no author software artifact was located.
weights_status: Hosted frontier model APIs; no task-finetuned weights. Immutable provider snapshots are not bundled with an artifact.
evaluation_route: Paper describes the full workflow, prompts, datasets and F2P outcome; SWT-Bench-Verified result is 77.8%. Without source, scripts, exact dataset manifests, cached outputs or a reproducibility package, a faithful rerun cannot be checked from public artifacts. An independent custom-model evaluation would need an implementation and is outside the current authorization. No code/API/model was run.
blockers: No public author implementation/evaluator or pinned source snapshot was located.
Main evaluation uses SWE-bench-derived Python datasets, not the user's primary Defects4J/BugsInPy setting; SWT-Bench is a secondary reported result.
Exact paper models are hosted Claude frontier APIs, with no immutable model snapshot or cached outputs verified.
A local custom-model evaluation requires an implementation and adaptation; this would not reproduce the paper and is not authorized as reimplementation.
concept_fit: High methodological relevance: directly targets F2P reproduction tests and studies whether mutation-derived execution feedback improves test selection. It offers useful prior art for evaluating oracle/test quality. It does not give root-cause labels or explanations; mutants are local rule-based variants of suspected functions, not historical fault causes.
recommendation: Keep as a high-priority conceptual comparator for the SWT-Bench reproduction-test direction, but do not select as the runnable/reproducible base. For an executable Defects4J evaluation foundation, #74 is stronger: it has direct buggy/fixed Defects4J data and public MIT analysis/source. For this user's concept-guided root-cause thesis, EvoOtter is useful related work on feedback signals, not an RCA method. No reproduction or implementation performed.
supporting_locations: Paper abstract and Sections I/III: formal F2P task, workflow, localization, mutation fitness and crossover.
Paper Section IV-E and Table VII: TDD-Bench-Verified, SWE-Rebench and SWT-Bench-Verified results; SWT-Bench result 77.8%.
Paper Sections VI/VII: limitations and conclusion.
Official author homepage publication list: confirms paper identity but exposes no EvoOtter source link; targeted GitHub searches yielded no attributable repository.
